questions.stem: The officer of the watch gives a helm order. What must the helmsman do first?
options: Repeat the order word for word, then carry it out and report when done
Carry it out in silence so the officer is not distracted
Wait for the officer to repeat it a second time
Carry it out and report only if the ship does not respond
questions.explanation: The routine is repeat, carry out, report. The repeat-back lets the officer catch a mishearing at once. Silence leaves the officer unsure the order was understood, and reporting only on failure skips the confirmation that the order has been completed.

options: Hold the rudder in the fore-and-aft position
Steer for the middle of the channel
Hold five degrees of rudder to starboard
Stop the engines
questions.explanation: Midships is the zero rudder angle: the rudder lies fore and aft. It has nothing to do with channel position, it is not a rudder angle to one side, and it is a wheel order, not an engine order.

questions.stem: The order is "Hard-a-starboard". What is the correct rudder position?
options: Fully over to starboard
Twenty-five degrees to starboard
Fully over to port
Five degrees to starboard, then midships
questions.explanation: Hard-a-starboard means the rudder is held fully over to starboard, the ship's limit. It is not fixed at 25 degrees (the stepped orders go only up to twenty-five), and it never means port.

questions.stem: The ship is turning to port with port twenty on. The officer orders "Ease to ten". What does the helmsman do?
options: Reduce the port rudder to ten degrees and hold it
Put on starboard ten to stop the swing
Put the rudder amidships
Put on ten more degrees of port rudder
questions.explanation: Ease to reduces the rudder to the stated angle on the same side. Starboard ten would be a different order; midships is a different order; adding rudder is the opposite of easing.

questions.stem: Which pair correctly matches an order with its meaning?
options: Meet her: check the swing of the ship's head in a turn
Meet her: bring the ship alongside the other vessel
Steady: steer the course on the chart
Nothing to port: hold port rudder
questions.explanation: Meet her asks the helmsman to check the swing, usually with some opposite rudder. It does not refer to another vessel. Steady means reduce the swing as quickly as possible, and Nothing to port means do not let the head go to port, not hold port rudder.

questions.stem: The ship is steering 088 and swinging slowly to starboard. The officer says "Steady as she goes" when the compass reads 092. What should the helmsman steer?
options: The heading the compass shows at the time of the order, 092
The original course, 088
The next round number, 095
Midships and no particular heading
questions.explanation: Steady as she goes means steer a steady course on the heading shown when the order is given, so 092. Going back to 088 would be a new course order. The helmsman then reports the heading he is steadying on.

questions.stem: A pilot with a different first language boards a Canadian vessel and the bridge team does not share another common language with the pilot. In what language must the pilot and bridge watchkeepers communicate on board?
options: English
The language of the ship's flag state
The language the pilot prefers
Whatever the master chooses, in writing, for each pilot
questions.explanation: The Navigation Safety Regulations, 2020, s. 137(3) require English for communications between the pilot and bridge watchkeeping personnel unless the people involved share another language. Here they do not, so English applies. The master records the general working language, but that choice does not override the English rule for pilot communications.

questions.stem: Scenario: the OOW says "Port fifteen." The helmsman replies "Port fifteen, sir" and turns the wheel. Five seconds later the rudder angle indicator still shows zero and the ship's head has not moved. What should the helmsman do?
options: Tell the OOW at once that the ship is not answering the wheel
Turn the wheel harder and say nothing until it responds
Wait for the OOW to notice and repeat the order
Put the wheel amidships and wait for the next order
questions.explanation: The standard phrase is to report if she does not answer the wheel. An unresponsive rudder is a steering failure or control problem, and the OOW must know immediately to start the emergency steering procedure. Staying silent, waiting, or centring the wheel all waste time.

questions.stem: Which wording belongs to standard IMO and Canadian helm orders?
options: Starboard ten
Right ten
Right rudder ten
Come right ten
questions.explanation: Standard wheel orders say port and starboard. Right and left rudder are common in United States training texts but are not the SMCP form and should not be mixed with it on the same bridge.

options: No more steering is needed
The helmsman has completed his turn at the wheel and a relief has arrived
The rudder is jammed
Steer by autopilot only
questions.explanation: In the SMCP list it means no more steering. It is not a report of a jammed rudder (that is reported by saying she does not answer the wheel), and it does not by itself say who will steer next.
